newsitem.title: CHINA: U.N. chief to attend Hong Kong handover ceremony.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief to attend Hong Kong handover ceremony.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan has accepted an invitation from Chinese President Jiang Zemin to attend a ceremony marking the return of Hong Kong to Beijing rule at midnight on June 30, Chinese radio said on Friday.

The end of British colonial rule in Hong Kong was an important event in Chinese modern history and a major international event, Jiang told Annan, who is visiting China for the first time since being appointed U.N. chief last December.
The territory would be China's bridge to the rest of the world and would maintain its prosperity and stability for a long time, state radio quoted him as saying.

Annan said on Thursday Chinese leaders had assured him of Hong Kong's future prospects by pointing out that if Beijing had wanted to harm the territory's interests, it could have done so many years before the end of British colonial rule.
He also praised China for supporting reform of the United Nations.
"I'm leaving encouraged that China supports the reform process," he told a news conference after meeting Jiang and Foreign Minister Qian Qichen.
China was contributing to the debate on reform of the United Nations and its leadership on the issue was felt throughout the global organisation, he said.
Annan on Friday left Beijing for the ancient capital of Xi'an, where he was scheduled to tour the city's famous buried terracotta warriors.
The U.N. chief was expected to end his five-day China visit on Sunday after visiting Shanghai.
